symbols.name: input precision
symbols.meaning: The number of fractional bits in each input coefficient.
symbols.quote: Inputs lie in $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with modulus at most 1, where $p$ is the number of fractional bits in each input coefficient.

symbols.name: size parameter
symbols.meaning: The size parameter of the network, which bounds the number of selected address bits.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the size parameter of the network, which bounds the number $D$ of selected address bits, and let $C_0$ and $C_1$ be constants fixed by the network construction.

symbols.name: network constant
symbols.meaning: A constant fixed by the network construction, scaling the depth bound.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the size parameter of the network, which bounds the number $D$ of selected address bits, and let $C_0$ and $C_1$ be constants fixed by the network construction.

symbols.name: depth exponent constant
symbols.meaning: A constant fixed by the network construction, used as the exponent of the size parameter in the depth bound.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the size parameter of the network, which bounds the number $D$ of selected address bits, and let $C_0$ and $C_1$ be constants fixed by the network construction.

symbols.name: guard count
symbols.meaning: The number of extra bits reserved beyond the input precision, per component, so that every intermediate coefficient is exact.
symbols.quote: The guard count $\Delta = \lceil C_0 d^{C_1} \rceil$ bounds the depth of every intermediate coefficient.

relations.quote: A guard-width bound is an explicit number of extra bits that bounds the intermediate coefficients of a [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) and makes them exact, so that one truncation at the end suffices.
The guard-width bound limits the denominators of the [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md) that appear as intermediate coefficients.
